subject: Sunset shift — handover ambiguity between CET and AEST for next week's demo
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orbitanalytics.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.nguyen@orbitanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 13:10:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Demo next week — quick timezone check

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for scheduling the demo with Redwood. Quick heads-up: our team is in Madrid (CET) and Tom is currently traveling back to Sydney (AEST). When we opened the invite it looks like Google converted the slot differently for each of us and the calendar shows a 10:00 start for me but 19:00 for Tom — that can't be right for a live walkthrough. We also noticed the invite timestamp is on the day DST shifts for our partner in APAC, so there's risk of an off-by-one-hour.

Could we confirm the intended timezone (CET or UTC) and, if possible, pick a slot that's within reasonable hours for both teams? Our preferred windows: 09:00–11:30 CET or 07:00–10:00 AEST, but flexible if we pick something that keeps the overlap in normal working hours.

I've attached a short agenda and a .ics with the ranges we can do.

Apologies for the scramble — travel + DST makes everything shakier than usual.

Best,
Marta
Head of Data Partnerships
Orbit Analytics

Attachments: orbit-demo-agenda.pdf (pdf), proposed-times.ics (calendar)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orbitanalytics.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo next week — quick timezone check

Hi Marta, Tom — thanks for flagging this.

Short answer: the original invite was set to Europe/Paris (CET/CEST) and Google is doing local conversions which, combined with the APAC DST boundary this week, created the mismatch. We'll standardize on UTC in the body of the invite and send a fresh calendar event with explicit UTC start/end times to avoid client conversions.

Proposed concrete options (all times in UTC):
- Option A: 2026-05-11 08:00–09:00 UTC (09:00–10:00 CET / 18:00–19:00 AEST)
- Option B: 2026-05-11 14:00–15:00 UTC (16:00–17:00 CET / 01:00–02:00 AEST next day — not ideal for Tom)
- Option C: 2026-05-12 07:00–08:00 UTC (08:00–09:00 CET / 17:00–18:00 AEST)

Given travel and usual work hours, I think Option A or C keep the overlap reasonable. Soojin, Jonas — can you confirm presenter availability for those slots?

I'll attach a fresh .ics with UTC-only times and add a note in the description: "All times shown in UTC — please don't rely on local auto-conversions."

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: demo-utc-invite.ics (calendar)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@orbitanalytics.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@orbitanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 01:12:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Demo next week — quick timezone check

Thanks Lauren. Quick note from ops: I'm in Seoul this week and scheduled to present the model walkthrough, so Option C (2026-05-12 07:00 UTC) works best for me — it keeps it earlier evening here and solid morning in Madrid.

One operational ask: can we lock the demo language and the dataset snippet ahead of time? If Tom will be remote from Sydney with limited bandwidth, we'll avoid a live large-file sync and use the small onboarding dataset instead (see slide 3 in the attached agenda).

Also flagging our fallback policy: if travel or connection drops, we can record the session and do a follow-up Q&A aligned with Tom's local morning next day.

Sooj
Senior Solutions Engineer

Attachment: small-sample-dataset-readme.txt (txt)
